subject: On‑prem activation validation & IP routing post‑check
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria@acmehealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Dan O'Neill <dan.oneill@cloudops.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem activation validation & IP routing post‑check

Sergio — thanks for the quick handoff this morning. We finished the initial smoke tests on the application tier in the DR rack and saw the following: TCP health checks for inference service on 10.10.5.12:8080 passed, but the metadata endpoint (10.10.5.12:8081/health) returned 503 for ~3 minutes during cache warmup.

We collected the following artifacts and attached them: a short runbook log and the VPC postcheck spreadsheet. A couple of asks before we close the window today: 
- Can your team confirm the egress SNAT IP mapping for the private subnet (we expect 35.198.11.22) so our external telemetry can be allowed?
- We saw intermittent TCP retransmits between the on‑prem LB and model shard leader; wondering if path MTU or an MTU mismatch is in play.

Happy to jump on a 20m call if that helps.

Maria
Lead Cloud Ops, Acme Health
[Attachment: runbook_playback_log_20260805.txt (text)]
[Attachment: acme_vpc_postcheck_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gomez <maria@acmehealth.com>, Dan O'Neill <dan.oneill@cloudops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem activation validation & IP routing post‑check

Thanks Maria — appreciate the notes and artifacts. Quick responses inline below and next steps at the bottom.

- SNAT IP: confirmed. Our NAT gateway for the private rack is using 35.198.11.22 for outbound connections. We pushed the allowlist change for your telemetry host (telemetry.acmehealth.com) at 10:45 PDT; can you confirm your side sees that source IP?

- TCP retransmits: agree this looks like transient MTU or path queuing. Action we took: lowered jumbo MTU to 9000->1500 on the infra switch connecting the LB and model nodes and reapplied offload settings on the LB. We also toggled TCP window scaling to the recommended profile for high token throughput. Please verify load/latency over the next hour.

- Metadata 503 during warmup: this matches expected behavior during KV cache priming when large batch priming runs. We added a temporary 2‑minute traffic hold in the routing policy to avoid user traffic until priming completes.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Maria/Acme: confirm telemetry host sees 35.198.11.22 as source for outbound probes (reply to thread).
2) Marissa & Karthik: schedule a 20m bridge to watch packet captures and BGP route table if retransmits persist.
3) Mina: if we still see 503s after priming, can you share the model shard logs and the KV cache warmup timeline?

I attached the postcheck snapshot of the firewall ACL for visibility.

Sergio
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: fw_acl_snapshot_20260806.json (json)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria@acmehealth.com>, Dan O'Neill <dan.oneill@cloudops.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem activation validation & IP routing post‑check

Looping in the ops playbook notes from the runbook playback we ran at 07:00 PDT. Summary: all primary smoke tests passed end‑to‑end after the infra MTU change; one followup remains on route propagation to the edge firewall when we fail traffic over to secondary fabric. Details below with excerpts from runbook_playback_log_20260807.txt: 

--- runbook excerpt ---
07:00 CHECK: LB health endpoints (8080/8081) x5 -> PASS (average latency 12ms)
07:05 CHECK: Model shard leader election -> PASS (leader = shard‑2, stable)
07:07 CHECK: KV cache warmup -> COMPLETED (2:30 elapsed)
07:10 CHECK: External telemetry egress -> FAILED initially (source IP 35.198.11.22 blocked by edge FW) -> RULE ADDED: allow telemetry.acmehealth.com from 35.198.11.22
07:12 CHECK: External telemetry egress -> PASS
07:20 FAILOVER TEST: reroute to secondary fabric -> WARNING (routes learned on secondary not present in edge FW for ephemeral SNAT pool)
--- end excerpt ---

Action items: 
- Karthik: please push the ephemeral SNAT pool entries for the secondary fabric into the edge firewall API. Attachment 'acme_vpc_postcheck_sheet.xlsx' has the expected ranges.
- Mina: please compress and attach the model shard logs for 07:00–07:15 PDT to this thread (we'll need them for the postmortem).
- Maria: confirm Procurement sees no outstanding billing hold so we can finalize the activation billing milestone.

I recommend we schedule a 30m closeout call at 11:00 PDT to validate the failover scenario once the firewall entries are present.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gomez <maria@acmehealth.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Dan O'Neill <dan.oneill@cloudops.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem activation validation & IP routing post‑check

Thanks everyone — quick status after the closeout play: 

- Firewall entries pushed for the secondary fabric ephemeral SNAT pool at 10:15 PDT via edge API. Verified via edge API and traceroute from a secondary LB: source shows 35.198.11.22 and telemetry host responded.
- Failover scenario exercised twice (manual failover + automated route flap). Services remained healthy; average end‑to‑end latency increased from 14ms -> 26ms during failover but returned to baseline within 40s.
- Attached compressed model logs for 07:00–07:15 (see attachment stub). Reduced metadata 503s: the final mitigation was extending the priming hold to 3 minutes for large batch priming.

Closing notes: this completes the post‑activation validation checklist. Recommend signoff from Acme on the activation milestone so we can move billing to "Activated" and remove the temporary traffic hold.

Karthik Iyer
Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: model_shard_logs_0700-0715.tar.gz (archive)]
